why: A (universes at 0) is the twelve step lemmas of Theorem 11.6.6 (1): well-definedness of H (mor_conj, hMor_src/tgt), steps (A)-(C) (surjective_hObj, isLocalScDiffeo_hObj, isScDiffeo_fibredMap_hFunctor, finite_fiber_hObj, isProperMap_hObj), three general lemmas (IsScDiffeoOn.restrictTarget, IsLocalScDiffeo.evenlyCovered_of_isProperMap, IsProperCovering.isProperMap), and the assembled isProperCovering_hFunctor_of. B says that for an equivalence Γ there is an EpFunctor H : P → Q with the entries of (11.18), (11.19), and that it is a proper covering. A ⇒ B: take H = hFunctor (the entries hold by rfl) and use isProperCovering_hFunctor_of, with hΨ, hΦ and hs taken from the fields of Γ.IsEquivalence. B ⇒ A fails for a real reason. isProperCovering_hFunctor_of is more general than the text's (1): it needs only Ψ, Φ local sc-diffeomorphisms on objects and Ψ onto on the fibres, not Γ an equivalence. And the general lemmas and the separate steps do not follow from B. What B does give is A's main conjunct in the text's case Γ an equivalence (B_to_isProperCovering_hFunctor', rt_check OK), since B's H is hFunctor by EpFunctor.ext.
